The diagram shows a sector, $EOG$, of a circle, with centre $O$ and radius $r$ cm. The line $GF$ is a tangent to the circle at $G$. Point $E$ is the midpoint of $OF$.

figures.cap: right triangle OGF with sector EOG of radius r cm and shaded region between arc GE and GF, EF

parts.latex: Find the expression for the exact area of the shaded region.

solutions.latex:
$OG=OE=r$ (radii of the circle) and $OE=EF$ ($E$ is the midpoint of $OF$), so $OF=2r$.

$\angle OGF=90^\circ$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius). By Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle OGF$:
$$\begin{aligned}GF&=\sqrt{OF^2-OG^2}\\&=\sqrt{(2r)^2-r^2}\\&=\sqrt{3}\,r\end{aligned}$$
Using the cosine ratio in $\triangle OGF$:
$$\cos\angle GOE=\dfrac{r}{2r}=\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\therefore\angle GOE=60^\circ=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area of }\triangle OGF&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times\sqrt{3}\,r\times r\\&=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\,r^2}{2}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area of sector }OGE&=\dfrac{60}{360}\pi r^2\quad\left(\text{or }\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\times\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\\&=\dfrac{\pi r^2}{6}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area of shaded region}&=\triangle OGF-\text{sector }OGE\\&=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\,r^2}{2}-\dfrac{\pi r^2}{6}\\&=\dfrac{(3\sqrt{3}-\pi)r^2}{6}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area BKQ} &= \dfrac{1}{2}(5-x)^2\times\dfrac{\pi}{3} \\ &= \dfrac{\pi}{6}(5-x)^2 \end{aligned}$$
For equal areas:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{x^2}{12} &= \dfrac{(5-x)^2}{6} \\ x^2 &= 2(5-x)^2 \\ &= 2(25 - 10x + x^2) \\ x^2 - 20x + 50 &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
By the quadratic formula:
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{20 \pm \sqrt{400-200}}{2} \\ &= 10 \pm 5\sqrt{2} \end{aligned}$$
So $x \approx 2.9289$ or $x \approx 17.07$.

K lies on AB, so $0<x<5$; reject the larger root.

The diagram below shows a circle of radius $r$ and centre $O$. The angle $AOB=\theta$.

\exfigure{1315_q26_1}

The length of the arc $AB$ is $30\,cm$. The area of the sector $OAB$ is $300\ cm^2$.

Find the values of $r$ and $\theta$.

solutions.latex:
The arc length and sector area formulas give two equations.

$$\begin{aligned}r\theta&=30 &&(1)\\ \dfrac12 r^2\theta&=300 &&(2)\end{aligned}$$

From (1), $\theta=\dfrac{30}{r}$. Substitute into (2).

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac12 r^2\left(\dfrac{30}{r}\right)&=300\\ 15r&=300\\ r&=20\end{aligned}$$

Then $\theta=\dfrac{30}{20}$.

$$\therefore\ r=20 \text{ cm},\quad \theta=1.5 \text{ rad } (\approx 86^\circ) \text{ (accept either)}$$
criteria: Provides both simultaneous equations, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula for a triangle, $A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 6\times 6\times\sin 30^\circ \\ &= 9 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} A_{\text{segment}} &= A_{\text{sector}} - A_{\text{triangle}} \\ &= \pi\times 6^2\times\dfrac{30}{360} - 9 \\ &= 3\pi - 9 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Area} = (3\pi-9) \text{ cm}^2 \ (\approx 0.425 \text{ cm}^2)$$

\exfigure{1274_q18_1}

The diagram shows a sector with radius $r$ and angle $\theta$ where $0<\theta\le 2\pi$. The arc length is $\dfrac{10\pi}{3}$.

figures.cap: sector with radius r, angle theta, arc length 10pi/3

parts.latex: Find the value of $\theta$ and hence, show that $r\ge\dfrac{5}{3}$.
Calculate the area of the sector when $r=4$.

solutions.latex:
The arc length formula is $l=r\theta$, with $0<\theta\le2\pi$.

$$\dfrac{10\pi}{3}=r\theta,\ \text{so } \theta=\dfrac{10\pi}{3r}$$

Now use $0<\theta\le 2\pi$.

$$\begin{aligned} 0<\dfrac{10\pi}{3r} &\le 2\pi \\ 10\pi &\le 6\pi r &&(\text{multiply by } 3r>0) \\ \dfrac{5}{3} &\le r &&(\text{divide by } 6\pi) \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ r\ge\dfrac{5}{3}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us.

solutions.latex:
The area of a sector is $A=\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta$, where $\theta=\dfrac{10\pi}{3r}$ and $r=4$.

$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times4^2\times\dfrac{10\pi}{3\times4} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times16\times\dfrac{10\pi}{12} \\ &= \dfrac{80\pi}{12} \\ &= \dfrac{20\pi}{3} \end{aligned}$$

The area of the sector is $\dfrac{20\pi}{3}$ square units.
criteria: Substitutes into the area formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
An annulus sector is made with an angle $\theta$ at its centre. Its inner and outer radii are $\dfrac{1}{r}$ metres and $r$ metres respectively, as shown.

\exfigure{1286_q15_1}

The perimeter of this annulus sector is 6 metres.

Show that $\theta=\dfrac{2(-r^2+3r+1)}{r^2+1}$.

solutions.latex:
The perimeter is two straight edges of length $r-\dfrac{1}{r}$ plus the inner arc $\dfrac{1}{r}\theta$ and the outer arc $r\theta$ (arc $=$ radius $\times$ angle).
$$P=2\left(r-\dfrac{1}{r}\right)+\dfrac{1}{r}\theta+r\theta$$
Set $P=6$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{2(r^2-1)}{r}+\dfrac{\theta}{r}+\dfrac{r^2\theta}{r}&=6\\2r^2-2+\theta+r^2\theta&=6r\\\theta(1+r^2)&=-2r^2+6r+2\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta=\dfrac{2(-r^2+3r+1)}{r^2+1}$$
criteria: Significant progress in simplifying the equation, or equivalent merit
Forms the equation for the perimeter, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: circle centre O, tangent AT, shaded region between AT, arc AB and BT

parts.latex: Express the area of the shaded region in terms of $r$ and $\theta$.
Given that $r=3$ and $\theta=1.2$, find the perimeter of the shaded region. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

solutions.latex:
$OA\perp AT$ since $AT$ is a tangent, so in right-angled triangle $OAT$, $\tan\theta=\dfrac{AT}{r}$.

Hence $AT=r\tan\theta$.

The shaded area is the triangle minus the sector.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area}&=\text{area }\triangle OAT-\text{sector }OAB\\ &=\dfrac12\times r\times r\tan\theta-\dfrac12r^2\theta\\ &=\dfrac12r^2\tan\theta-\dfrac12r^2\theta\end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
The perimeter is $AT$, $BT$ and the arc $AB$.

In right-angled triangle $OAT$, $\cos\theta=\dfrac{r}{OT}$, so $OT=\dfrac{3}{\cos1.2}$, and $BT=OT-OB$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Perimeter}&=AT+BT+\text{arc }AB\\ &=3\tan1.2+(OT-OB)+3\times1.2\\ &=3\tan1.2+\left(\dfrac{3}{\cos1.2}-3\right)+3\times1.2\\ &\approx16.5955\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{perimeter}\approx16.60 \text{ cm}$$
criteria: Finds $AT$, $BT$ and the arc length, or equivalent merit

$$\begin{aligned} A_{RPQ}&=\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta \\ &=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 60^2\times\theta \\ &=1800\theta \end{aligned}$$
The sector $RXY$ has half this area, with radius $r=RX$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 1800\theta \\ \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta&=900\theta \\ r^2&=1800 \\ r&=30\sqrt{2} \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.
